preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner (or gain ownership through social engineering/compromise)
Attacker must hold some TeaToken balance to demonstrate the fee impact

violation_target.exploit_hint: As owner, call setTaxFeePercent() and setLiquidityFeePercent() with extremely high values (e.g., 99 each). Then perform token transfers to collect excessive fees into the contract address. The contract will accumulate fees and eventually swap them for ETH via swapAndLiquify, with liquidity added to the owner. Alternatively, set fees to 100 to make transfers impossible, disrupting the token's functionality.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The TeaToken contract allows the owner to set tax and liquidity fees up to 100%. By setting both to extremely high values (e.g., 99% each), transfers will incur nearly 100% fees. These fees accumulate in the contract and are eventually swapped to ETH and added as liquidity, with liquidity tokens going to the owner. This allows the owner to extract value from all token transfers.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Become the contract owner via storage manipulation. 2. Set both taxFee and liquidityFee to 99. 3. Transfer tokens between accounts to generate massive fees. 4. Trigger swapAndLiquify to convert fees to ETH/liquidity for the owner.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Overwrite owner storage slot to make attacker the owner. 2. Call setTaxFeePercent(99) and setLiquidityFeePercent(99). 3. Get some TeaToken balance for a victim address. 4. Transfer tokens from victim to another address to generate fees. 5. Ensure contract has enough tokens to trigger swapAndLiquify. 6. The owner (attacker) will receive liquidity tokens when swapAndLiquify executes.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The contract is a reflection token with fee-on-transfer. When owner sets fees to 99% each, transfers incur ~198% fees (impossible, would revert). Actually, fees can't exceed 100% total. Need to set fees to something high but not impossible. Also, the owner is excluded from fees by default in constructor.
attempts.attack_strategy: 1. Get current owner address. 2. Impersonate owner using vm.prank. 3. Set taxFee to 49 and liquidityFee to 49 (total 98%). 4. Transfer tokens between non-excluded addresses to generate fees. 5. Fees accumulate in contract and can be converted to liquidity for owner.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get owner address via interface call. 2. Start prank as owner. 3. Set fees to 49 each. 4. Create test addresses and give them tokens. 5. Perform transfers to generate fees. 6. Check that contract accumulates fees.
attempts.failure_reflection: The previous PoC had potential issues: 1. Using raw .call() instead of interface calls. 2. Storage slot manipulation might be incorrect. 3. Network errors might be due to too many RPC calls. 4. Need to handle the reflection token mechanics properly.
